units.spine: Carts stopped on this spot before any stall did, and the stalls came afterwards to the carts.
The rules in this town have rooms a traveller can find, the hall and the courthouse and the customs house.
People can afford to argue about something other than money.
No one has to explain why a town stands on this ground.
The walls are sound and the watch walks its circuit, and neither of them is for show.
The townsfolk do not expect this town to lose a straight fight, and they say as much to its neighbours.
Against the beasts of this ground the town has men who know the work and the tools the work takes.
Order holds on the main streets and thins in the lanes behind them.
Prices hold from one market to the next, and the town is not living on the last thing it sold.
For magic the town has an alchemist's shop and no more, and whatever it wants past that comes from outside.
The price of bread is watched here, as it is not in a town at ease.
What stands to change hands between The Governing Council and The Order of the Watch is political influence, and the two are careful with each other.
Traffic runs past this town on the road and leaves very little of itself behind.
Everything the town cannot grow comes in on the road and comes in no other way.
Spitzplatz is a town in the plain meaning of the word.
One tie carries more weight than the rest, and the weight shows in what the town refuses.
Ties here are the ordinary ones, work and family and the same streets.
